g.text: VIP Customer Service: From Arrival to Payment (Stage 2)
Illustrative scenario: a VIP arrives in Turn 1 and chooses Pasta.
Actual arrivals and food choices may differ between runs.
Restaurant, staff and menu are already initialized.
The full game runs for 18 turns.
Only key interactions in this scenario are expanded.
TURN 1: VIP ARRIVAL AND SEATING (FULL TURN)
All tables are empty at the start of Turn 1.
readyToPayLine.poll() is null; no diner finishes eating.
From Turn 2 onward, repeated turn-start calls,
CLI input parsing, table validation, ordinary WAIT,
end-turn display and routine satisfaction scans are omitted.
Only new actions and significant state changes are expanded.
TURN 2: VIP ORDERS PASTA AND CHEF PREPARES UNIT 1

a.title: order
a.text: != null and status is WAITING or PREPARING

g.text: End Turn 2: VIP waits for Pasta, 95 to 90 satisfaction.
Waiter chooses WAIT; action handling is as in Turn 1.
Customer selection, getOrder() and status checks
repeat Turn 2 and are not redrawn.
End Turn 3: VIP waits for service, 90 to 85 satisfaction.
Pasta is READY for the Waiter's next turn.
TURN 4: MANAGER PRIORITIZES SERVICE OR SEATING
As in Turn 1, the scheduled new customer
is created and added to the waiting queue.
One Waiter action is spent serving VIP.
New customer remains QUEUING and loses
As shown in Turn 1, seat newcomer at Table 2.
TURN 5: SEAT CUSTOMER 2; VIP FINISHES EATING
VIP is EATING at the start of Turn 5.
Customer 2 is seated at free Table 2.
Seating steps are the same as Turn 1; omitted.
No unprepared orders exist on this selected path.
Chef WAIT follows the procedure shown in Turn 1.
VIP is not in the payment queue yet.
TURN 6: VIP PAYMENT WHILE RESTAURANT CONTINUES
Waiter may TAKE_ORDER from the new customer
at Table 2; Chef may PREPARE that order.
These actions do not prevent automatic VIP payment.
Cashier processes one payer independently of Waiter.
Turns 7 to 18 repeat the established game flow.
